# Table

## Summary
A sortable record table over cards the consumer already holds. Columns are declared as `{ key, label, align?, width?, showAbove?, sortable?, value(item), sortValue(item) }`: the value function reads whatever the consumer wants (fields, computed values, linked traversals), so which of a card's forty fields belong in the table is the consumer's design decision, not a flag's guess. Click a header to sort; when the display value is formatted (money, dates) give the column a `sortValue` returning the raw number, because formatted strings do not order correctly. Sorting is applied to the whole set before paging.

## API
- `@items`, `@columns`, `@emptyMessage`, `@caption`, `@rowKey`.
- `@onRowClick(item)`: the first cell holds a real button whose hit area is stretched across the row, so a row is one tab stop and a screen reader hears a control, not a row pretending to be one.
- `@rowClass(item)`: a per-row class for state at the row edge (`sev-over`, `sev-note`, `sev-ok`, `sev-cool` ship as severity stripes).
- `@pageSize`: opt-in pagination; the pager always states the true total.
- `showAbove: 480 | 640 | 720 | 900` on a column hides it below that container width, as a real container query.
- Controlled sort: pass `@sortKey`, `@sortDescending` and `@onSort(key)` and the table reflects the consumer's order instead of sorting again.
- `<:cell as |item column|>`: a column with no `value` is rendered by this block, which is how a consumer yields pills or atoms into cells. Set `custom: true` on a column to route it through the block while still supplying `value` or `sortValue`, so a custom cell can sort or fall back to text.

## Usage
```gts
import { Table, type TableColumn } from '@cardstack/catalog/components/table';

columns: TableColumn[] = [
  { key: 'title', label: 'Task', value: (t) => (t as Task).title },
  { key: 'due', label: 'Due', showAbove: 640,
    value: (t) => (t as Task).dueDate?.toLocaleDateString(),
    sortValue: (t) => (t as Task).dueDate?.getTime() },
];

<Table @items={{this.tasks}} @columns={{this.columns}} @pageSize={{25}} @onRowClick={{this.open}} />
```
The linked example mounts this table and the Board over the same task records, with Status and Priority atoms yielded into cells and a severity stripe driven by due date.

## Non-goals
Filtering (consumers pass a filtered array; filters are app state). Virtual scroll. Bulk selection and bulk actions. Inline editing (the platform edit format's job). Query-driven loading: this table takes resolved instances; pointing at a card type and deriving columns from its schema is a different block.
